title: Filters and Routers
summary: Filter = gate pass/stop; Router = directs to different paths based on conditions

sections.heading: Orientation — Lesson Start
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Automation becomes useful when you choose the path based on conditions — not when everything goes in a single line.
- Why now? After Triggers and Actions, you need to differentiate: Price inquiry ≠ Complaint ≠ Follow-up — each has a different response.
- What after the lesson? You will add one if/then to your workflow: If [condition] → [path or action].

sections.heading: Tension — A Familiar Situation
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- "Same response for all messages" — and the customer is angry.
- You have automation responding to WhatsApp messages. Someone asks about the price — they receive "Thank you for reaching out." Someone complains — the same response.
- The repetitive work is not the problem — the issue is that the workflow has no decision: everything is in the same path.
- The default worker needs to know: When to continue? When to stop? When to go to another path? — This is the job of the Filter and Router.

sections.heading: Core Idea — Filter = Gate. Router = Fork in the Road
sections.subtitle: Filter = Gate. Router = Fork in the Road
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Filter: If the condition is met → data passes. If not → workflow stops here. Example: "If a phone number is found → continue."
- Router: Same as Trigger, but it branches into paths based on conditions. Example: Price → Sales path. Complaint → Support path.
- One if/then changes the customer experience — from a general response to a case-appropriate response.
- Start with one clear condition — not 10 branches from day one.

sections.heading: Comparison — One Path vs. Conditional Paths
sections.subtitle: One Path vs. Conditional Paths
sections.contentMarkdown:
| One Path for Everything | One if/then |
|-------------------|--------------|
| Every lead receives the same email and response — the complaining customer feels unheard. | If the message contains "Price" → send a price list. Otherwise → forward to support. Each case has an appropriate response. |

sections.heading: Glossary — Two Terms for Paths
sections.subtitle: Two Terms for Paths
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| Filter | Gate: condition met → passes. Not → stops | If there is no email in the form → do not complete registration |
| Router | Fork in the road: same Trigger, different paths based on condition | VIP → special message. New customer → welcome message |

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: A customer spent over 5000 EGP → special thank you email. Under 5000 → regular email. What is more appropriate?
Router differentiates based on purchase value — two different paths
Explanation: You need two different paths based on the condition — this is a Router. Filter stops or passes, but does not distribute.

sections.heading: Mission — Add one if/then to the workflow
sections.subtitle: Add one if/then to the workflow
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: The mission is design — not mandatory building. Choose a recurring workflow and add one condition that changes the path or stops execution. AI can suggest wording — you choose the final version. Submission: Workflow · Trigger · if/then (condition, then, else) · example input for each path Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Clear condition | 50% | One specific if/then — not vague language; the condition is testable (yes/no) |
| Different paths | 50% | Then and else actually do something different; example input for each path |
